title: Reduction-Aware Directive-Based Programming via Multi-Dimensional Homomorphisms
problem: Traditional directive-based models (OpenMP, OpenACC) struggle with reduction-intensive computations and fail to deliver consistently portable performance across CPU and GPU architectures.
motivation: Reduction operations are ubiquitous in scientific computing (linear algebra, data mining, quantum chemistry) but are poorly optimized by generic directive frameworks. A specialized abstraction is needed to enable both high performance and programmer productivity.
method: Introduce a novel directive design grounded in Multi-Dimensional Homomorphisms (MDH) formalism, explicitly tailored for data-parallel tensor expressions. Implement in Python-based framework supporting CPU and GPU backends with portable collective communication via OMPCCL.
key_novelty: MDH-based directive design for reduction-heavy tensor computations; portable performance across CPU/GPU; Python host language for programmer productivity.
contributions: MDH-based directive specification for data-parallel tensor computations
Portable performance across CPUs (Intel MKL/oneMKL) and GPUs (NVIDIA cuBLAS/cuDNN)
5x speedups on CPUs and 2x on GPUs vs. vendor libraries
Python language integration for enhanced programmer productivity
limitations: Performance claims against vendor libraries may not account for all optimization techniques; specific hardware generations tested not detailed in abstract; generalization to non-reduction operations unclear.
